title: #robertdowneyjr #broadway #theatre #mcneal #reviews #fyp
transcript: Robert Downey Jr is currently starring in a play on Broadway and people are not really liking it I finally saw it this weekend and I'm not gonna defend it exactly but I am gonna give some credit where it's due RDJ himself gives what I thought was a pretty strong performance as this a-hole writer figure who is using AI to write his work but also taking things from people in his life so it sets up this reasonably thought provoking parallel between regular old plagiarism and AI plagiarism like as much as we think of AI as a threat in and of itself and it is in many ways the play also reminds us that at the core of the issue are also the human beings who are exploiting it for their own personal gain this character archetype that he's playing here is one that we've seen a lot in media maybe too much And a lot of the time even if it's like a tragic figure and it's commentary you can usually tell that the writer almost always the male writer just like kind of secretly admires the character a little bit more than they should they'll be like “this guy's an a-hole, but damn he's a genius!” and you'll be like “oh?” and they'll be like “what? I said he's an asshole!” And it's like “ok,  but you sure do love writing about these a-holes over and over again, don't you?” Akhtar does deviate from this trope in the sense that like McNealc is not really a genius like he's kind of a fraud, so like I don't think the playwright has that much respect for him as a person or as an artist teamatically that's kind of an improvement but as an audience member watching it it doesn't actually help that much cause either way you slice it watching this character spend 90 minutes being a piece of sh!t and then self destructing is just not that interesting like I don't think Akhtar condones this character's behavior but he still makes us sit and listen to him pontificate with these long winded speeches about the state of the world and the state of writing There’s still just this “back in my day” “old man yells at cloud” energy to these scenes that is boring not literally boring, like it held my attention but boring in a deeper sense but what was just as damning to me about the play if not more so was the side characters to be clear I'm not always bothered by thinly written side characters and I do think that such a protagonist driven character study like this is one of the cases where it doesn't actually matter that much but the writing for these characters wasn't just thin it was kind of actively bad and so was the way that they were directed There was something weirdly unserious and goofy and amateurish about the way that they were presented and it really seemed like they were just maybe not given any direction at all one of the things that I almost gave this play credit for is that it's probably the only piece of media I've seen that actively comments on this trend that we've seen in like post Me Too Hollywood where all of these male writers are conspicuously trying to course correct by writing about female characters and feminist themes a lot more but they're doing it in such a hollow thin way that is just regurgitating talking points that have already been said much better by actual women this play explicitly comments on that and yet it falls into that trap itself because all of these women surrounding this male protagonist are written so terribly and because this play is kind of meta and self aware in some ways you could spend days tying yourself into knots talking about “that was the point! that was the point!” “its commentary! its commentary!” but at the end of the day it just doesn't work that well
reasoning: The reviewer gives credit to RDJ's performance and acknowledges some thematically interesting ideas, but ultimately finds the play uninteresting, with poorly written and directed side characters, and concludes 'it just doesn't work that well.' The review leans negative overall, stopping short of recommending it.
